title: Celeriac mash
summary: Celeriac and cauliflower simmered until soft and mashed with butter, cream, thyme and nutmeg: earthy, faintly celery-sweet and good with a roast.

ingredients.note: peeled and cut into 2 cm (3/4 in) cubes

steps: Put the celeriac and garlic in a pan, cover with cold water, add the salt and bring to a boil. Simmer 10 minutes, then add the cauliflower and simmer 10–12 minutes more, until everything is very tender.
Drain well and return to the hot pan over low heat for 1–2 minutes, shaking, to drive off excess water.
Mash or blend with the butter, warm cream, thyme, nutmeg, salt and pepper until smooth. Taste for seasoning and finish with chives.
dairy_free_notes: Dairy-free butter and coconut milk make a slightly looser mash with a hint of coconut sweetness; it pairs well with the nutmeg.
tips: Peel celeriac with a knife, not a peeler: cut off the knobbly skin and roots generously.

origin.history: Celeriac is a form of wild celery bred for its swollen root, grown in Europe from around the 1600s and especially popular in France, Germany and Central and Northern Europe as a winter vegetable that stores well. Purée of celeriac, often mixed with potato, became a classic French accompaniment to roast meat and game, and is now a common Christmas side.
